summary: The review's deterministic floor now lists the risky areas a change touches (replication and sync; store schema, trim and checkpoints; concurrency; CI and signing stages; wire types between versions) and says when a MEDIUM change in one needs a Factory read before it is queued. The areas never change the risk level. scripts/review-risk prints factory_read and needs_factory_read, the verdict schema and validator accept risk.deterministic.factory_read and risk.needs_factory_read as optional fields, the runner records them and prints 'needs Factory read (areas)', and docs/review.md states the rule.

replay.detail: Review tooling and documentation only (.st/review-risk.json, .st/review-verdict.schema.json, scripts/review, scripts/review-risk, scripts/review-validate, their tests and docs/review.md); no protocol, schema, policy, workflow or note change outside the review's own files.

schema.detail: The review verdict schema gains two optional fields (risk.deterministic.factory_read, risk.needs_factory_read); older verdicts still validate and the runner leaves the fields out when the base's review-risk does not report them.

rules.detail: The review rules gain a factory_read list in .st/review-risk.json (five risky areas) and docs/review.md states the lane rule it encodes: a MEDIUM change in one of those areas does not self-queue and goes to Factory for one read. The owner approved it through ask step-run/ask-781daf9db23755ab7edfc6a63eb13950/ask. The risk levels, risky-classes.json and the low/high routing are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Local review tooling only; nothing outside it reads the new fields.

manual.detail: An author whose MEDIUM change touches one of the factory_read areas sends the signed head to Factory for one read before queueing; nothing else to do at deploy.
